items.title: Comparison of an object supported on a closed subset inside an open with its restriction and its extension by zero
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter cohomology.tex (Cohomology of Sheaves)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file cohomology.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: For an open subspace j: U to X and a closed subset T of X contained in U, the lemma shows that an object of the derived category whose cohomology sheaves are supported on T is unchanged by the derived pushforward of its restriction to U, and that for an object of the derived category of U supported on T the extension by zero and the derived pushforward agree (statement lines 8297-8307). The proof sets V to the complement of T and W to U cap V, so that X is the union of the two opens U and V, and then checks the two assertions by restricting to U and to V: on V both the derived pushforward and the extension by zero vanish because the objects restrict to zero there, while on U both agree with the original object (proof lines 8309-8323). The restriction formula for the pushforward of a restriction along an open immersion is the single cited input. The claim is H2: a short two-open localization argument in which the closedness of T is exactly what makes the complement an open on which everything vanishes.
